 PHI

 Player Stats

 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said that Jabari Walker will start at center for the injured Joel Embiid (foot) on Sunday against the Pacers. 
 Due to injury management reasons, Embiid will not play on Sunday. Walker has been tabbed to fill the void, making him worth considering for streaming. Nurse also said that LeBron James and Dean Wade should also see time at the five in smaller lineups. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Pacers. 
 LeBron will be back for the first leg of the 76ers’ back-to-back. Dean Wade started in LeBron’s absence on Thursday, but with Joel Embiid (foot) ruled out on Sunday, Wade could remain the starter if they choose to start LeBron at center, which they did in one of Embiid’s two other absences this season.

 Forward-Center

 Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Dean Wade and Joel Embiid will start against the Raptors on Thursday. 
 Wade will get the starting nod with LeBron James sidelined. This will likely be a singular start for Wade, though the 76ers do have a back-to-back coming up on Sunday and Monday, so Wade could be in line for another start.

 LeBron James (sciatica) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Raptors. 
 James, who struggled in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics, is back on the injury report to manage his sciatica. With Joel Embiid (foot) also questionable, the 76ers could be without two starters on Thursday. If LeBron sits, Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope should see their roles expand.

 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid (foot) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Raptors. 
 While Embiid appeared to tweak something in his left foot/ankle during Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics, his right foot has been an issue for longer. If he can’t play on Thursday, the 76ers could move Dean Wade into the starting lineup, while Jabari Walker would take on more responsibilities.

 PHI 
 Forward 
 #30 
 Adem Bona (spine) is out for Thursday’s game against the Raptors. 
 Thursday’s game will be the fourth game Bona has missed due to a cervical spine sprain. Jabari Walker has taken on a slightly larger role, but not enough to make him a must-roster player in redraft leagues. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James amassed 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics. 
 James, who was inadvertently raked across the face by Paul George early in the fourth quarter, struggled against the Celtics. The good news for fantasy managers is that he committed just one turnover, but the 41-year-old shot the ball poorly. James, who entered Tuesday’s game shooting 25 percent from three, made just one of six three-point attempts. With the 76ers counting on Tyrese Maxey to be their lead scoring option, James’ ability to hit perimeter shots takes on added importance, and he’s struggling right now.

 #30 
 Adem Bona (spine) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Bona will miss a third straight game with a cervical spine sprain. His absence has increased minutes for Jabari Walker, who isn’t worth streaming unless Joel Embiid is out. Embiid is not on the injury report for Tuesday, so there’s no need to roster Walker. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James accounted for 22 points (8-of-16 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Bulls. 
 After scoring eight points in a poor showing against the Cavaliers on Friday, James benefited from facing one of the NBA’s worst defenses on Sunday. The 41-year-old forward shot well and finished with his second game with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists this season. The 76ers play three games next week with no back-to-backs, which should help James get his rest.
